text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning.

- Norway's District Attorney could decided to withdraw an extradition demand to the Netherlands for anti-whaling activist Paul Watson if Dutch authorities keep him in custody for a long period. Watson was convicted in Norway to 120 days imprisonment after attacks against whaling ships.
- Environment Minister Thorbjoern Berntsen was the only politician at a meeting in pariliament on Monday to fully support the government's plans to build two gas-fired power plants.
- The Nordic countries have decided to cooperate in order to control gambling on the Internet and machines.

- The cost of the two planned gas-fired power stations could be twice as high as first estimated if Naturkraft, the company set up to build the plants, is forced to develop a purification plant for carbon dioxide.
- Tiger Management of the United States sold its stake of 8.4 million shares in Norwegian Seafoods to Aker RGI on Monday under a share options scheme.
